name: boobrie

attributes.attribute: sometimes appears as a cow or water horse
haunts lakes and cries like a strange bird
preys on calves, lambs, and otters

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The boobrie is a Scottish folkloric figure. Its other name is tarbh boibhre. This Highland specter changes its shape. It sometimes appears as a cow. At other times it is a water horse. On occasion it takes the form of a huge insect. That insect has long tentacles. It sucks the blood of horses. The boobrie haunts lakes. It cries like a strange bird. Its common form is a waterbird. That bird is far larger than any duck or swan. Its footprint is the size of a large deer's antlers. It preys on calves and lambs. This makes it a danger to subsistence farmers. When cattle are absent it eats otters.

okr.objective: Describe the boobrie as the shape-shifting specter that preys on farm livestock.
key_results: The boobrie appears as a cow, water horse, or a huge insect.
It commonly takes the form of a waterbird far larger than a swan.
The boobrie haunts lakes and cries like a strange bird.
It preys on calves, lambs, and otters.
